nodes.description: Public string state variable holding the current quiz question.
Address state variable storing the account that started the game; used as an access-control guard in StopGame and NewQuestion.
bytes32 state variable holding keccak256 hash of the expected answer; controls whether Play pays out.
Public payable function that initialises question, responseHash and questionSender only when responseHash is still empty.
External payable function that checks require(msg.sender == tx.origin), compares keccak256(_response) to responseHash and, if msg.value > 1 ether, sends the whole contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable function restricted to questionSender that transfers the entire contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable function restricted to questionSender that replaces the question and responseHash.
Payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers without any logic.
Caller-supplied address; used for authorisation checks, ownership assignment and as payout recipient.
Transaction origin used in Play as an anti-contract guard (require(msg.sender == tx.origin)).
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Play: external call sending the full balance before any state update (reentrancy surface).
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame: external call sending the full balance to questionSender.
String parameter _question of StartGame, written into the question state variable.
String parameter _response of StartGame, hashed with keccak256 into responseHash.
String parameter _response of Play, hashed and compared against responseHash to authorise payout.
String parameter _question of NewQuestion, written into the question state variable.
bytes32 parameter _responseHash of NewQuestion, written into the responseHash state variable.

edges.reason: StartGame assigns msg.sender to questionSender, so an untrusted caller becomes the privileged owner of the game.
StartGame writes questionSender, establishing the access-control identity used by StopGame and NewQuestion.
StartGame writes the _question parameter into the question state variable.
StartGame writes keccak256(_response) into responseHash.
Parameter _question of StartGame flows into the question state variable.
Parameter _response of StartGame is hashed and stored in responseHash.
Play enforces require(msg.sender == tx.origin), making transaction origin a security-relevant condition.
Play branches on msg.sender equality with tx.origin before allowing execution.
Play reads responseHash and compares it with keccak256(_response) to decide whether to pay out.
Parameter _response of Play is hashed and compared against the responseHash state variable.
Play reaches msg.sender.transfer(this.balance), forwarding the contract balance to the untrusted caller.
The balance transfer in Play invokes the recipient (msg.sender), which may re-enter Play or the fallback before state is settled.
StopGame reads questionSender to enforce require(msg.sender == questionSender).
StopGame follows the same full-balance payout pattern as Play, providing a reentrancy path.
StopGame reaches msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside the authorised branch.
The balance transfer in StopGame invokes msg.sender, creating a callback into the contract.
StopGame's require depends on the untrusted msg.sender matching questionSender.
NewQuestion reads questionSender to enforce require(msg.sender == questionSender).
NewQuestion's authorisation check depends directly on the untrusted msg.sender.
NewQuestion overwrites the question state variable.
NewQuestion overwrites the responseHash state variable with a caller-supplied hash.
Parameter _question of NewQuestion flows into the question state variable.
Parameter _responseHash of NewQuestion flows directly into responseHash.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter _question only exists as the input of StartGame and should be folded into that function node.
Parameter _response of StartGame is hashed into responseHash and has no independent semantic identity.
Parameter _response of Play is only used for the hash comparison that gates the payout in Play.
Parameter _question of NewQuestion is a plain input stored by that function.
Parameter _responseHash of NewQuestion is a plain input stored into the responseHash state variable by that function.
